notes: FROZEN (daemon=incapable, route=frozen) — no phases, per the SKILL frozen rule. The CORRECT spec, asserted here and never weakened to the daemon limit: with the backchannel toggle on and hermes' 'control' permission granted on a session hosted by a readable backend (the driver already launches `hermes chat` under tmux), the session traces ready -> working (a prompt driving the terminal tool at a Tier-2 dangerous command) -> waiting for as long as hermes' TUI-only approval modal is on screen -> working when the user answers it -> ready at settle; structured metrics (tokens/cost) are unchanged by the terminal-derived signal, and the waiting state is not double-counted. HERMES CANNOT BE OBSERVED FOR THIS TODAY, for two independent reasons. (1) Consent gate: core/application/services/terminal_observer.go observe() returns at its first statement unless consent.Granted(adapter, ControlPermissionKey) — and core/adapters/inbound/agents/hermes/agent.go declares exactly one permission (observe-kind 'store') with agent.Control left at its zero value ON PURPOSE (see the Agent() doc comment). permission.Set.Get defaults an unanswered pair to StatePending, and PermissionService's grant-all branch iterates only a.Permissions, so Granted("hermes","control") is false in EVERY mode including IRRLICHT_PERMISSION_MODE=grant-all; Snapshot() likewise never offers a 'control' row for hermes. CaptureScreen is therefore never called for a hermes session, DetectUI never runs, and no waiting edge can exist. That is the scenario's own negative acceptance criterion ('Nothing is read back when ... control is not granted for the agent'), so it is an adapter-declaration limit, not a daemon bug. (2) Marker gap: core/domain/backchannel/uidetect.go's trustDialogMarkers hold three Claude Code phrases plus mistral-vibe's two, and hermes' rendered panel matches none of them — its title is '⚠️  Dangerous Command' with options 'Allow once' / 'Allow for this session' / 'Add to permanent allowlist' / 'Deny' (cli.py v0.19.0 approval-panel renderer, blocking on a queue.Queue with a 300s fail-closed deny). Even with control granted, DetectUI would return UIKindNone — the same shape mistral-vibe's 6.2 cell had before #988 added its markers. The agent side is NOT the blocker: the modal is real, default-on, blocking, and invisible to the only Source this adapter watches (2.19 pinned that the assistant/tool_calls row is flushed before dispatch, so the state.db tail while blocked is byte-identical to a slow tool). Driver side is a third, lesser gap: answering the modal needs a keystroke and the hermes driver stubs `keys` (DRIVE_ELICITS="send slash sleep wait_turn"). UNBLOCK = declare Control{SupportsInput}+agent.ControlPermission() on hermes/agent.go (the follow-up its own comment defers) AND add hermes' panel marker to uidetect.go AND port `keys` — all three, or the first recording verifies PARTIAL. No observations block is asserted: a frozen cell is never recorded and a doc-guessed model pin would only fail a future verify.
